markdown:
# Methodology

How Spin ID defines and computes everything, for coaches and analysts. This page grows with
each phase. Sections marked *Planned* describe the spec; they become "Implemented" with test
results when the phase that builds them is done.

Data: MLB Statcast via Baseball Savant.

## Conventions (implemented as configuration in Phase 0)

- **Units.** Velocity in mph, spin in rpm, movement in inches (one decimal), angles in degrees, release positions in feet, accelerations in ft/s².
- **Handedness.** All comparisons happen in right-handed space. Left-handers are mirrored when data loads; the true hand is kept for display.
- **Movement direction.** Induced vertical break (IVB) is positive when the pitch rides. Horizontal break (HB) is positive toward the arm side.
- **Tilt.** The direction of spin-induced movement, read as a clock face from the pitcher's side: 12:00 is pure backspin, 3:00 is pure arm side. Stored in degrees clockwise from 12:00 (30° per hour), shown as a clock time to the nearest 15 minutes.
- **Measured vs. observed tilt.** Measured tilt comes from the spin axis Hawk-Eye measures. Observed tilt is the direction the ball actually moved. The Spin ID uses measured tilt; the difference is the seam effect.

## Data (implemented in Phase 1)

**Sources.** Pitch-by-pitch Statcast data for MLB regular-season games, 2021–2026, from Baseball
Savant's Statcast Search, one day per request. Baseball Savant's Active Spin, Spin Direction, Arm
Angle, and Pitch Movement leaderboards, per season (and per pitch type where offered). 2020 is
left out because the season was short.

**Handedness.** Left-handers are mirrored into right-handed space when the data loads: every
left-right quantity (release side, horizontal movement, horizontal velocity and acceleration,
plate location) changes sign, and the spin axis becomes 360° minus itself. The true hand is
kept for display. After mirroring, a left-hander's four-seam runs to the arm side exactly like a
right-hander's.

**Tilt.** Statcast's spin axis is reported from the catcher's view, with 180° at pure backspin.
Tilt on the pitcher's-side clock is `(spin axis − 180) mod 360` degrees clockwise from 12:00
toward the arm side. Check: the median four-seam reads about 1:00 and the median curveball about
7:15 for both hands. (Savant's Spin Direction leaderboard can be shown "from the pitcher's view";
those numbers are the mirror image, 360° minus the axis.)

**Measured vs. observed tilt.** Measured tilt comes from the spin axis Hawk-Eye measures (the
pitch-level axis matches Savant's "measured" column within about 2°, not the "inferred" one).
Observed tilt is the direction the ball actually moved, from horizontal and induced vertical
break. Observed minus measured is the seam-effect deviation.

**Movement.** Computed the same way for every source, from the nine-parameter trajectory fit
(release velocity and constant acceleration in three directions):

1. Time at release: solve for when the ball is at 60.5 ft minus extension.
2. Time at the front of home plate: solve for when it is at 17/12 ft.
3. Flight time T = plate time − release time.
4. Induced vertical break = ½ (vertical acceleration + 32.174 ft/s²) T² × 12 inches.
5. Horizontal break (arm side positive) = −½ × horizontal acceleration × T² × 12 inches.
6. Approach angles: the direction of travel at the plate (negative vertical angle = descending).

The accelerations include drag's small cross-components; they are not corrected. Because the
same spin produces about the same inches at any velocity (flight time shrinks as speed grows),
Spin ID compares pitches in inches, and the inspector can show the acceleration equivalent.

Our movement correlates with Statcast's published movement (`pfx`) at about 0.998 and runs
about 7% larger. Statcast doesn't document exactly which part of the flight `pfx` covers, so we
report the difference instead of guessing at its cause, and use our own definition everywhere so
every source (Statcast and TrackMan) is measured the same way.

**Location-adjusted VAA.** A higher pitch arrives flatter. Within each pitch type and season,
vertical approach angle is regressed on plate height and side; the adjusted value is the VAA the
pitch would have at that group's average location.

**Quality.** Pitches missing velocity, spin, extension, or any trajectory value are left out of
shape calculations (and counted). Guards: velocity 40–106 mph, spin 300–3,800 rpm, movement
within 30 inches. Knuckleballs, eephus, unknown, and intentional-ball codes are ignored.

**Run value.** Statcast's `delta_run_exp` is positive when the batting team gains
(strikeouts average about −0.22 runs, home runs about +1.5), so pitcher run value is its negative.

**Data Health.** Settings > Data shows pitches and pitchers per season, the share of pitches
with each field, leaderboard files, and plain-English warnings.

## The Spin ID (implemented in Phase 2)

A pitcher's Spin ID describes the reference fastball: four-seam if thrown at least 100 times in
the season, otherwise sinker, otherwise cutter. With 50–99 of the chosen pitch the ID is
**Provisional** (shown with a dashed outline); with fewer than 50 of all three, there is no ID and
the screen says why.

| Field | Meaning | Shown rounded to |
|---|---|---|
| Slot | Arm angle (0 sidearm, 90 overhead) | 5° |
| Efficiency | Active spin, the share of spin that moves the ball | 5% |
| Tilt | Measured tilt compared with the tilt that slot usually produces (+ rides over the slot, − runs under it) | 5°, always signed |
| Spin | Bauer units: spin rate ÷ velocity | 1 |

Rounding is for display only (half away from zero). Families and all math use exact values.

**Expected tilt for the slot.** Pitchers from higher slots spin their fastballs closer to 12:00.
For each reference type, a curve of measured tilt against slot is fitted to the 2023–2025 pool
(every pitcher-season with 100+ reference pitches): 1,487 four-seam, 298 sinker, 32 cutter
pitcher-seasons. Natural cubic splines (3–5 knots) and a smoothed isotonic fit compete on 5-fold
cross-validation and the most accurate wins (four-seam: spline, 6.6° scatter; sinker: isotonic,
7.5°; cutter: spline, 17.7°, thin data). The curve is stored in the schema as a table every 0.5°
of slot and held flat beyond its ends.

**Tilt offset** = expected tilt − measured tilt, wrapped to −180°…+180°. Positive means the spin
sits closer to 12:00 than the slot predicts: the fastball **rides over the slot**.

**Families** (15 = 5 slot bands × 3 tilt groups):
- Slot bands are the pool's quintiles: Low under 29°, Low-Mid 29–36°, Mid 36–43°, Mid-High 43–48°, High 48° and up.
- Tilt groups use the 20th and 80th percentiles of the pool's tilt offset, separately for each reference type: four-seam −5.2° / +4.9°, sinker −6.4° / +5.9°, cutter −11.5° / +10.3°. At or above the high cutoff is "+" (rides over), at or below the low cutoff is "−" (runs under), between is true to slot.

**Efficiency** is the Active Spin leaderboard's percentage for the reference type, or the Spin
Direction leaderboard's active spin when the first doesn't list it. **Spin** is Bauer units: the
reference pitch's average spin rate ÷ average velocity.

**Percentiles and words.** Each field's percentile ranks a pitcher among full IDs with the same
reference type that season. The one-line description turns percentiles into words: low (under
20), below average (20–40), average (40–60), above average (60–80), high (80+).

These fits and cutoffs were frozen as **ID Schema v1 on 2026-10-11** (now `config/id_schema_v1.yaml`).
Changing any of them means a new schema version, a migration, and a DECISIONS entry. Details and
the spot check: DECISIONS D-201–D-214. Schema v2 replaced v1 on 2026-10-14 (next section).

## ID Schema v2: the fastball by spin, spin direction corrected for cut (Phase 8c)

Kade asked (2026-10-14) for the ID fastball to be chosen by how it spins, and for the climb in spin
direction that comes with cutting the ball to be taken out. The plan was committed before any number
was computed (`docs/lab/physics-2-and-schema-v2-plan.md`).

**The ID fastball.** A tagged four-seam or cutter over 60% efficiency counts as a four-seam (the
more-thrown one if both); sinkers keep their tag. Four-seam with 100+ pitches, else sinker; 50–99 is
Provisional. A fastball that spins like a cutter (60% or less) gives no ID.

**The ID's spin direction**, in three steps:
1. *Measured:* Statcast's spin direction (the 3D spin axis drawn on the catcher's x–z plane).
2. *Gyro leak out (physics-2):* the gyro part of the spin points along the flight, a few degrees
   off that plane, so a slice of it shows in the drawing, more as efficiency drops (four-seams: 0.8°
   at 94%+, 1.4° at 88–94%, 2.0° at 80–88%, 2.6° at 60–80%). Physics-2 solves for the transverse
   direction alone.
3. *Cut correction:* + k × (reference efficiency − efficiency). k is measured within pitchers: the
   same pitcher's fastball from one season to the next, change in direction on change in efficiency
   and change in slot. Four-seams: **0.538° per point** (95% range 0.500–0.576; 874 season pairs);
   sinkers 0.485° (0.422–0.547; 375 pairs). On the reported direction (before step 2) it is 0.477°,
   because the leak tilts the reported direction back the other way. Reference efficiency = the v2
   pool's median: 91.7% four-seams, 84.6% sinkers.

Example: a four-seam at 80% efficiency at 1:00 (30.0°) after step 2: 91.7 − 80 = 11.7 points ×
0.538 = +6.3°, so 36.3° (about 1:13). The Families page shows this math with the data behind it, and
each pitcher's inspector shows their own numbers. Athletes skip step 2 (TrackMan's spin axis isn't
Statcast's drawing).

**Frozen 2026-10-14 (v2).** Expected direction by slot refit on the ID direction (four-seam scatter
5.8°, was 6.6°; sinker 6.7°, was 7.5°); tilt groups at the pool's 20th/80th percentiles: four-seam
−4.9° / +4.8°, sinker −5.8° / +5.2°; slot bands unchanged. A cutter curve (transverse direction, 422
cutters by spin) is kept for slot changes on cutters only.

**Do the families still work?** T1 on Schema v2 passed with T1's pass lines: year to year r 0.93,
odd vs. even games 0.99, slot changers 0.27 (`docs/lab/T1v2.md`). 74.5% of pitchers kept their
family; four-seams under 85% efficiency read "rides over" 41.5% of the time in v1 and 19.7% in v2
(`docs/lab/schema-v2-migration.md`). DECISIONS D-861–D-868.

Text forms: `2+ | 30/80/+10/25` (copy), `2+ | Slot 30° · Eff 80% · Tilt +10° · Spin 25 BU`
(long), and a spoken form for screen readers.

## Comparing pitches (implemented after Phase 2 review)

Pitch design talks about secondaries relative to the fastball, so every pitch is also shown as a
difference from a comparison pitch: the four-seam when it's thrown 50+ times, otherwise the Spin ID's
fastball, otherwise the most-thrown pitch, or any pitch the coach picks. Differences are this pitch
minus the comparison pitch: speed (mph), IVB and HB (inches), spin rate (rpm), spin direction (clock
time, 30° per hour), and release height (inches).

The Spin ID itself can also be built from another fastball the pitcher throws 50+ times, with the
same frozen schema. That's a view for coaches; the standard ID (the reference rule's pick) is the one
used for families, lists, comps, and validation.

## Validation: T1, ID Stability (implemented in Phase 3)

Pre-registered on 2026-10-11 (thresholds confirmed by Kade, committed before any stability number
was computed). Uses the standard Spin IDs from ID Schema v1, 2021–2026.

- **Year to year:** pitchers with 300+ of the same reference fastball in back-to-back seasons.
  Tilt offset correlation r = 0.92 (95% range 0.91–0.94; 992 pairs, 471 pitchers). Pass line 0.60.
- **Odd vs. even games:** each qualifying season split into alternating games, each half measured
  like a season. r = 0.99 (0.991–0.993; 2,030 pitcher-seasons). Pass line 0.80.
- **Slot changers:** pairs whose slot moved 5°+; the typical offset change was 0.34 times the
  typical slot change (0.29–0.40; 123 pairs). Pass line 0.5 or less.

**Passed.** Efficiency (r = 0.94) and Bauer units (r = 0.94 year to year, 0.99 odd vs. even) were
reported but didn't decide the gate. Limitations: only high-volume pitchers; the odd/even check
shares a season's conditions; the expected-tilt curve was fitted to seasons inside the test window.
Full report: `docs/lab/T1.md`; the Lab screen shows every point.

## Physics: spin-only movement and seam effects (implemented in Phase 4; physics-2 in Phase 8c)

**Physics-2 (in use since 2026-10-14).** Following George Lewis's "Public Statcast Non-Magnus
Modeling": the flight is stepped from release to the plate every 2 ms with gravity, drag (drag
coefficient 0.320, read from every pitch's own trajectory), and Magnus lift with the spin in 3D (the
transverse part along the spin direction, the gyro part along the flight). Lift: Nathan's prescription
A, C_L = 0.336 × (1 − e^(−6.041 S)) × efficiency. One scale (0.964) fitted on the same 1,070
four-seams as physics-1. It replaced physics-1 by the rule written before it ran: cross-validated
error 0.91 in against 1.15 in (`docs/lab/physics-2.md`). Made-up pitches (What-If, Potential) fly
along their pitch group's typical direction from their own release; that agrees with their own flight
within 0.23 in. Physics-1, below, is kept for the record.

**Spin-only (Magnus) movement.** From velocity, spin rate, efficiency, and measured tilt: transverse
spin ω_T = e·ω, spin factor S = r·ω_T / v, lift C_L = S / (2.32·S + 0.4), Magnus acceleration
a = ρ·π·r²·C_L·v² / (2m), movement M = ½·a·T² with T each pitch type's measured flight time, split by
tilt into IVB = M·cos θ and HB = M·sin θ. Ball 0.1453 kg, radius 0.0369 m, air 1.225 kg/m³.

**Calibration (model `physics-1`).** One scale factor fitted on 1,070 MLB four-seam pitcher-seasons
whose movement direction is within 5° of their spin direction (little seam effect): scale 0.887,
R² 0.57, residual SD 1.15 in. The model is about right for four-seams, sinkers, and changeups and
runs high for sliders, cutters, and curveballs, so seam effects are compared within a pitch type.
Flight-time fallback T = d / (k·v): k = 0.954 (R² 0.995).

**Seam vector** = observed movement minus spin-only movement (inches, vertical and arm side): the
part of the movement the spin doesn't explain (seam-shifted wake and similar). Every pitch card
shows it beside the league's typical value for that pitch type.

**Inches vs. acceleration.** Aerodynamic force grows with velocity squared while flight time
shrinks with velocity, so the same spin per mph and seam setup produces about the same inches at
85 or 95 mph, while acceleration (ft/s²) climbs with velocity. That is why the ID uses Bauer units
and comps and maps use inches. The inspector shows both for the reference pitch (a = 2·M / T²).

## Comps (implemented in Phase 4)

The comps for a pitcher are the MLB pitcher-seasons with the same reference fastball and a full ID
whose four ID numbers are closest. Each number is divided by its spread in the reference pool, then
weighted (slot 1, tilt 1, efficiency 0.75, spin 0.75); similarity = 100·exp(−d²/2). Each comp shows
once, at its closest season; 25 by default (10–50). What Comps Throw summarizes their pitches thrown
50+ times, each compared with that comp's own fastball. Comps are MLB pitchers who kept a pitch long
enough to log it, so reachable ranges lean optimistic.

## Stuff+ and Shape+ (implemented in Phase 5)

**Spin ID's own model. Not FanGraphs Stuff+.** Stuff+ estimates how hard a pitch is to hit from how
it leaves the hand and moves. It ignores location, count, and results.

**What it learns.** For every MLB pitch from 2021 to 2024, the target is the run value of that pitch
from the pitcher's side (the negative of Statcast's `delta_run_exp`). Three gradient-boosted tree
models (LightGBM) learn it: fastballs (four-seam, sinker, cutter), breaking balls, and offspeed.

**What it reads (model `stuff-1`).** Velocity (mph); vertical and horizontal movement as
accelerations, a_z = 2·IVB / T² and a_x = 2·HB / T² (ft/s², T = flight time); spin rate; spin
direction (as sine and cosine); release height and side, extension, arm angle; and whether the
batter stands on the same side. Non-fastballs also read their differences from the pitcher's
fastball that season (velocity, IVB, HB, spin direction), because a slider is judged against the
fastball it plays off. Left-handers are mirrored, as everywhere in the app.

**From a pitch to a number.** The model's prediction for each pitch is blended over batter side
using the league's same-side share for the pitcher's hand (right-handers 0.53, left-handers 0.27),
then averaged over the pitcher's pitches of that type in the season (S). Then

  Stuff+ = 100 + 10 × (S − μ) / σ

where μ and σ are the mean and standard deviation of S over the 7,319 pitcher-pitch-type seasons in
2021–2024 with 100+ pitches. 100 is the average pitch in those years; each 10 points is one standard
deviation.

**How it was tuned.** Settings (learning rate, tree size, minimum pitches per leaf) and whether to
read movement as inches or as accelerations were chosen on 2025 alone (706,038 pitches). The two
versions were nearly tied (mean squared error per pitch 0.0505675 with accelerations, 0.0505702 with
inches); accelerations were kept. 2026 was not looked at until the T5 test.

**Shape+** is the same model with every pitch at its group's league-average velocity (fastball 93.1
mph, breaking 83.0, offspeed 85.4), accelerations scaled to match, and its own μ and σ. It shows shape
and release without speed.

**Confidence.** A pitch is scored High, Medium, or Low by how many similar pitches the model learned
from: the mean distance to the 50 nearest of 150,000 training pitches (shape and release, each
scaled by its spread). High is within the closest 80% of training pitches' own distances, Medium
within 98%, Low beyond. Low-confidence numbers are dimmed and labeled.

**Drivers.** Each Stuff+ shows the three features that moved it most, from the model's own
per-feature contributions (SHAP values) converted to Stuff+ points.

## Potential: spin twins, seam effects, slot changes (Phase 5, revised after Kade's review)

**Spin twins.** For a pitch, the twins are other MLB pitchers' pitches of the same type with nearly
the same velocity (±1.5 mph), spin for the speed (±1.0 Bauer units), spin efficiency (±5 points), and
spin direction (±10°, 20 minutes on the clock). Distance is the root mean square of the four
differences in tolerance units; "tight" twins are within every tolerance. Each pitcher appears once,
at the closest season. With the spin matched, differences in movement are mostly seam effects (how
the seams disturb the air), plus measurement noise: tight twins typically differ by 1–3 inches. The
chart is TrackMan-style (horizontal break across, arm side positive for every pitcher; induced
vertical break up), in inches or as acceleration (a = 2 × movement ÷ flight time², ft/s²).

**Seam effects.** Movement from spin alone comes from the Magnus physics (above); the seam shift is
actual minus spin-only movement, compared with the typical shift for the pitch type (the physics runs
high on gyro-heavy pitches). The spin-direction deviation is the direction the ball moves minus the
direction its spin points (seam-shifted wake). "Same spin, better results" lists tight twins with
100+ pitches whose run value per 100 pitches is higher, and how their movement differs. Spin ID shows
that movement is available; it doesn't say how to grip the ball.

**Slot changes (fastballs).** The pitcher's spin rate, efficiency, velocity, seam effect, and tilt
offset stay; only the arm slot moves. New spin direction = expected tilt at the new slot (frozen ID
schema) minus the same offset; movement changes by what the spin-only physics says the new direction
does. Release height moves 0.30 in per degree (fitted on 1,403 real season-to-season slot changes).
Peers are real fastballs from within 3° of the new slot with similar spin for the speed, efficiency,
and offset; their median Stuff+ and run value show what this kind of fastball does from there.

## Potential: envelope, ceiling, gap, lever (implemented in Phase 5)

**Envelope.** For pitch type K, each comp who threw K 50+ times gives a recipe relative to their own
fastball: spin-direction difference, efficiency, spin ratio, velocity ratio, and seam vector. Each
recipe is transplanted onto the pitcher's fastball (tilt = fastball tilt + difference; spin =
fastball spin × ratio; velocity = fastball velocity × ratio), run through the spin-only physics, and
shifted by the comp's seam vector. The envelope is the 80% highest-density region of these candidate
shapes (weighted by similarity) on a 1-inch grid.

**Ceiling and best point.** Every grid cell inside the envelope is scored with Stuff+ at the
pitcher's release and the pitcher's own velocity, with spin and spin direction taken from the nearby
candidates. A thrown fastball keeps its natural spin rate, efficiency, and direction: only the comps'
seam effects vary. Shapes that score above the best real pitch of their type count as low confidence. Ceiling
= the 90th percentile of cells with High or Medium confidence; the best point (star) is the top one.
Low-confidence cells never set a ceiling and are hatched on the map.

**Gap and arsenal.** Gap = Ceiling − current Stuff+. Arsenal now = usage-weighted Stuff+; arsenal
ceiling = the same weights with each pitch at the higher of now and its confident ceiling. Pitches
thrown fewer than 50 times appear under Add a Pitch: Expected if Added is the median of the comps' real
Stuff+ on that pitch (ceiling: their top quarter), and a Best Addition must be thrown by at least a
fifth of the comps.

**Levers.** From the current pitch to the comp recipe nearest the best point, each change is applied
alone and rescored: spin direction (Hand Position at Release), efficiency (Spin Efficiency), spin
(Spin Rate on This Pitch), and seam shift (Grip / Seam Orientation). Fastballs keep their natural
spin, so their only lever is the seam shift; slot changes have their own view. The biggest
gain is the main lever. When it is grip, the seam percentile says where the pitcher's seam effect
sits among comps, measured along the direction that improves Stuff+.

**Confidence of a potential.** High: 15+ comps throw K and the best point has High support. Medium:
8+ comps and at least Medium support. Otherwise Low, shown as "Exploratory" first and never ranked in
Smart Lists.

## What-If (implemented in Phase 6)

**Controls.** Slot change (−20° to +20°) moves every pitch, because the whole arm moves. Efficiency
(±30 points), spin direction (±20°, + rides over toward 12:00), and velocity (±3 mph; spin rate stays)
change one chosen pitch. Ballpark: as pitched, a neutral park, or any MLB park. The sliders sit beside
the movement plot. Undo and Redo (⌘Z, ⇧⌘Z), saved scenarios, side-by-side comparison, and Reset.

**Physics mode.** Spin direction follows the slot one for one (a lower slot moves it toward 3:00);
efficiency, spin, and velocity stay unless their controls move; release height moves 0.30 in per degree
of slot (fitted on real slot changes).

**Efficiency moves spin direction too (Phase 8e).** When a pitcher cuts a pitch, its spin direction tips
toward 12:00. Measured on the same pitchers from one season to the next, with slot, speed, and spin held:
four-seams 0.45° per point, sinkers 0.40, cutters 0.43, sliders 0.66, splitters −0.33, sweepers −0.16
(changeups and curveballs don't move clearly, so they hold). The efficiency control carries that move; the
spin-direction control adds to it. Checked before it went in, on 1,477 real changes of 3+ points: the average
miss fell from 1.536 in to 1.520 in (cutters 1.55 → 1.41 in) (`docs/lab/efficiency-climb.md`). A seam
response learned from those same changes (movement-2) predicted worse than movement-1 and isn't used
(`docs/lab/efficiency-response.md`).

**Movement: the MLB movement model (`movement-1`).** A scenario's movement is the pitch's own movement
plus the change the model gives from today's inputs to the scenario's, so a scenario with no change is
exactly today. The model is spin-only physics plus the seam effect real MLB pitches show at the same
velocity, spin rate, efficiency, spin direction, and arm angle: a smooth weighted average over every
pitcher-season of that pitch type (14,402 pitcher-seasons, 4.1 million pitches, 2021–2026; the pitcher's
own seasons left out), weighted by how close each one is on all five and by its pitch count. Where few
MLB pitches are close, it leans on a wider neighborhood, so it never jumps; each scenario pitch says how
many similar pitcher-seasons are behind it (High 30+, Medium 10+, Low). This is why a 93% sinker that
loses efficiency gains sink and keeps its run until about 80%, and then the run fades, as MLB sinkers do;
spin-only physics would shrink both. Velocity alone (spin rate fixed) changes movement about 0.1 in per
mph, in the model and in real pitchers whose spin didn't change. Exploratory checks (not registered
tests): on 7,771 real back-to-back seasons, the model's movement changes missed by 1.1 in on average
(spin-only physics 1.6 in; no change 1.8 in); T3's computation rerun with it: Data-Driven 1.49 in vs.
2.24 in for no change (33% less error; T3 as registered, with spin-only movement: 28%).

**Ballparks (`parks-1`).** Measured from every pitch: movement = the pitcher's own average for the pitch
type and season + the park's effect for that pitch type, separated because pitchers throw in many parks.
0 is the average park. Thin air at Coors Field takes 3.2 in of IVB and 2.0 in of arm-side run off a
four-seam (−2.95 to −3.25 in every season 2021–2026) and shrinks every pitch's spin-induced movement
(curveballs drop 1.5 in less, sweepers sweep 2.2 in less). Every other park is within −0.5 to +1.4 in
for four-seams, steady from season to season (SD 0.22 in or less). A scenario in another park adds that
park's effect minus the parks the pitch was actually thrown in. Tampa Bay's 2025 season (Steinbrenner
Field) and the Athletics' 2025–2026 seasons (Sutter Health Park) are their own parks. Games at neutral
sites count toward the home team's park.

**Data-Driven mode.** A transition model learned from 983 real season-to-season fastball pairs whose
slot changed 3+ degrees: linear quantile regression (10th, 50th, 90th percentiles) of the change in spin
direction, efficiency, spin rate, velocity, release height, and extension, from the slot change, the
starting slot, and the starting value. The screen shows the median result with the 10th–90th range for
the reference fastball. In backtest T3 the range held 52% of real outcomes (target 80%), so real outcomes
vary more than it shows.

**Outputs.** The new Spin ID and family (frozen schema), every pitch's movement and Stuff+ (today's
Stuff+ plus the model's change for the new shape, with its confidence), and new comps.

## Validation: T2–T4 backtests (implemented in Phase 6)

Registered before running (commit 713e974); each ran once. Leakage: anything judged in season N+1 uses
only data through season N (Stuff+ trained on 2021–2024; comps and twins through 2025 for T2 and T4;
the transition model refit without the pitcher being predicted for T3).

- **T3 Slot-change prediction: passed.** On 390 real slot changes, Data-Driven movement error was 28%
  lower than assuming nothing changes (pass line 20%); Physics alone 24%.
- **T2 Seam-gap backtest: failed.** Of 33 Grip Candidates that changed shape, 58% landed inside their
  spin twins' 80% region (pass line 70–90%). They moved toward the better twins 64% of the time and
  gained 2.4 more Stuff+ than other pitches that changed (reported only, small sample).
- **T4 Gap predicts gains: failed.** Partial correlation of gap and next-season Stuff+ change,
  controlling for current Stuff+: 0.07 (95% range −0.05 to 0.19) among 318 pitches that changed shape.

Full reports: `docs/lab/T2.md`, `T3.md`, `T4.md`. Case Studies in the Lab show hits beside misses.

## Reports, exports, and the demo (implemented in Phase 7)

- **Pitcher Report:** one page (US Letter or A4) with the Spin ID, arsenal movement, every pitch's
  today and potential, the top three recommendations, the top five comps, and notes on confidence,
  Stuff+, and the tests behind it. Printed from the Report tab (Save as PDF in the print sheet).
- **Export Figure:** any chart in Light, Dark, or Shifted Wake, as PNG (2x or 3x, drawn at that
  resolution) or SVG, with its title, summary, and data note; Copy Chart puts it on the clipboard.
- **Figure Pack:** every Lab chart plus captions and case studies in one .zip.
- **Static demo:** the showcase pitchers, families, and Lab, precomputed, running from any static
  folder. What-If there is a precomputed grid (slot −15° to +15°, efficiency −10 to +10 points, steps of
  5). It never contains single pitches or amateur data.

## Amateur athletes (implemented in Phase 8)

Athletes are typed in by hand (each pitch type's averages, exactly as TrackMan shows them) or imported
from TrackMan files, and compared with MLB pitchers on every screen. They stay on this Mac.

- **Right-handed space.** TrackMan shows horizontal break and release side from the pitcher's view,
  positive toward third base, and spin direction on its clock (a right-hander's four-seam near 1:00, a
  left-hander's near 11:00). Spin ID turns these into the same right-handed space as MLB data (arm side
  positive, left-handers mirrored), so an athlete's pitch compares with any MLB pitch of either hand.
  A file's own signs are read from its fastballs (which way they run and spin), never assumed.
- **Spin ID.** Same frozen schema as MLB pitchers, from the four-seam (else sinker, else cutter).
  Provisional below 100 fastballs and whenever it rests on averages typed by hand; it still opens
  Comps, Potential, and What-If, labeled Provisional.
- **Arm angle without video** (`arm-1`): estimated from release height, release side, and the
  athlete's height, with geometry fit to 5,666 MLB pitcher-seasons of Hawk-Eye arm angle. Typical error
  7.3° (7.5° without height). Shown with "≈". An arm angle typed from video replaces it.
- **Efficiency without 3D spin:** the efficiency at which spin-only physics gives the pitch's
  movement (seam effects ignored). **Spin direction without 3D spin:** the direction the ball moved, so
  the seam effect is unknown.
- **Shape+ first.** Amateur velocity is outside the MLB range, so Shape+ (velocity set to the MLB
  average) leads; Stuff+ at the athlete's own velocity is shown beside it. Every athlete screen says:
  "Compared against MLB pitchers. Velocity and Stuff+ are outside the MLB range; use Shape+."
- **Nothing filled in silently.** Usage needs a count for every pitch type. A missing extension uses
  the MLB median for the pitch type (6.4–6.5 ft), labeled on the pitch. Each number that wasn't measured
  says where it came from on the pitch card.
- **Privacy.** A separate file on this Mac (`data/amateur.duckdb`); shown by name, initials, or a
  number; nothing printed or exported without the athlete's consent switch; never in the demo.

## Family Explorer (implemented in Phase 8b)

What each Spin ID family does with each pitch (Families > Explorer).

- **Pitches by spin.** Four-seams and cutters are grouped by spin efficiency, not by what they were
  called: over 60% is a four-seam, 60% or less a cutter (Kade's line; the data's natural gap between the
  two is at 62–66%). Efficiency is per pitcher, pitch type, and season (Baseball Savant). Other pitches keep
  their tags for now.
- **Families** are the Spin ID families (Schema v1), full IDs only, leaving out pitchers whose ID fastball
  spins like a cutter.
- **Numbers.** Each family's number pools every pitch of that kind its pitchers threw; the 95% range
  counts each pitcher once. Pitch results: Whiff Rate (misses per swing), CSW Rate, Called Strike Rate,
  Chase Rate, Zone Rate, Put-Away Rate (strikeouts per two-strike pitch), Run Value per 100; and shape:
  velocity, ride, run, efficiency, spin, slot, Stuff+, Shape+.
- **Views.** Report Card (each family on one stat for one pitch); Slot × Spin (a grid of any two of
  slot, efficiency, tilt offset, spin per mph, velocity, IVB, HB); Movement (each family's average shape);
  Strengths (differences that survive a check for flukes across every comparison, at a 5% false discovery
  rate). Strengths describe families; they don't show that spin causes the difference.

## Spin Brackets (Phase 8f)

Every pitch also gets a Spin Bracket: a name from what the ball does, not its Statcast tag (`spinid_core.brackets`,
frozen lines in `config/brackets.yaml`, version 2). The rules run in order:

1. Knuckleball: spin under 392 rpm.
2. Eephus: under 61.2 mph.
3. At fastball speed (within 2.6 mph of the pitcher's fastest pitch type):
   - Cutter at 60% efficiency or less (Kade, D-851, D-887).
   - Sinker when the seams move it 3.2°+ off its spin direction.
   - Otherwise Four-seam.
4. Gyro slider: under 3.0 in of total break.
5. Off-speed (3.4 in+ to the arm side): Splitter at 18.0 Bauer units or less, otherwise Changeup.
6. A slower Cutter: within 6.4 mph of the fastest pitch type, not dropping.
7. Breaking balls by total break (9.2 in) and direction (within 65.9° of straight down):
   - Curveball: big break, down.
   - Sweeper: big break, sideways.
   - Death ball: smaller break, down.
   - Slider: smaller break, sideways or up.

Where the lines come from:
- Lines between named groups are crossings: the point where each group's smoothed distribution is equally high.
  Each has a 95% range from 300 resamples of pitchers, with a valley as a check.
- The 60% line and the 3 in line are Kade's, checked against the data.
- The lines were fit on 2023–2025 pitcher-season pitch types with 100+ pitches, and each plan was committed
  before checking it on 2026: [plan](lab/brackets-plan.md), [report](lab/brackets.md), [second plan](lab/brackets-v2-plan.md),
  [report](lab/brackets-v2.md).

Agreement with Statcast tags is 88.5% in 2023–2025 and 86.9% in 2026. 90.2% of pitches land in the same bracket
the next season. A pitch inside a line's 95% range is a close call, and the app names both brackets. Pitch names
across the app follow the **Pitch Names** switch (Statcast Tags | Spin Brackets). Potential and What-If keep tags
because their models are built by tag, and they say which bracket each pitch is in.

model_cards.name: Physics-2: spin-only (Magnus) movement, flight integrated step by step
model_cards.data: 1,070 MLB four-seam pitcher-seasons (2021–2026, 100+ pitches) whose movement direction is within 5° of their spin direction (little seam effect). Chosen over physics-1 by the rule written before it ran (docs/lab/physics-2-and-schema-v2-plan.md; results in docs/lab/physics-2.md).
model_cards.features: Gravity, drag, and Magnus lift, stepped through the flight every 2 ms from the pitch's release. Spin in 3D: the transverse part along the spin direction with the gyro leak taken out, the gyro part along the flight. Lift: Nathan's prescription A, C_L = 0.336 × (1 − e^(−6.041 S)) × efficiency. Drag read from every pitch's own trajectory.

model_cards.name: What-If transition model (Data-Driven mode)
model_cards.data: 983 season-to-season fastball pairs (same pitcher and type, 100+ pitches both seasons) whose arm slot changed 3+ degrees, out of 3,022 pairs. Backtest T3 refits it leaving each pitcher out.
model_cards.features: Linear quantile regression (10th, 50th, 90th percentiles) of the change in spin direction, efficiency, spin rate, velocity, release height, and extension, from the slot change, the starting slot, and the starting value.

model_cards.name: What-If movement: the MLB movement model
model_cards.data: 14,402 MLB pitcher-seasons (4,100,939 pitches, 50+ per pitcher-season, efficiency and measured spin direction known), park effects removed. The subject pitcher's own seasons are left out.
model_cards.features: Spin-only physics plus the seam effect (observed − spin-only) of MLB pitches of the same type, weighted by closeness in velocity, spin rate, efficiency, spin direction, and arm angle (Gaussian kernels; smoothing chosen by leave-one-pitcher-out cross-validation, never below a floor that keeps sliders smooth) and by pitch count. Checks are exploratory, not registered tests.

model_cards.name: Stuff+ (Spin ID's own model. Not FanGraphs Stuff+.)
model_cards.data: 2,824,529 MLB pitches from 2021–2024 for training; settings and the acceleration choice were picked on 706,038 pitches from 2025. 2026 is held out for the T5 test.
model_cards.features: Velocity, induced vertical and horizontal break (as accelerations), spin rate, spin direction, release height and side, extension, arm angle, and batter side; non-fastballs add their differences from the pitcher's fastball. Target: run value per pitch (pitcher's view). Three gradient-boosted tree models: fastballs, breaking balls, offspeed.
